title: Intrinsic properties and point sets of morphisms of DM stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, maps over $S$, algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a DM stack $\mathcal X$, its points are its objects over spectra of fields in the scheme universe, identified by isomorphisms and field extensions (equivalently, the equivalence relation generated by arrows between such objects). A subset of points is closed exactly when its inverse image on every etale surjective scheme atlas is closed. A scheme point in a chart is represented by a field-valued point of that scheme. A stack morphism induces the map on point classes given by its functor on objects. Its relative diagonal sends $x$ to $(x,x,\mathrm{id})$ in its 2-fibre product with itself. A scheme-test property $P$ of a representable map means that every scheme 2-base change is represented, with its projection, by a scheme map with property $P$. A source-local algebraic-space-test property means that every scheme 2-base change is an algebraic space, with the specified projection, and every etale scheme chart of it has property $P$ over the test scheme. Here etale is [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A morphism of DM stacks is locally of finite type when the scheme projection from every etale scheme atlas of every scheme base change is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is quasi-compact if every affine scheme base change has a quasi-compact etale scheme atlas. It is universally closed if every scheme base change is closed on these point spaces; equivalently every algebraic-stack base change is closed on point spaces, since closedness is detected by atlases. It is proper if it is locally of finite type, quasi-compact, universally closed, and its relative diagonal is proper by scheme tests [def-weil-proper-morphism]; for DM diagonals this is equivalent to properness as an algebraic-space morphism, since a proper unramified algebraic space over a scheme is finite and hence a scheme. It is locally quasi-finite if it is locally of finite type, its relative diagonal is locally quasi-finite by algebraic-space tests [pqf-def-quasifinite], and every field fibre has discrete point space, expressed by closed complements of singletons. For a map $E\to F$ of algebraic spaces, ordinary chartwise local quasi-finiteness means local quasi-finiteness of every compatible map $U\to V$ between etale scheme charts of $E$ and $F$, without a surjectivity requirement on either chart. For the scheme base-change comparisons and representable etale maps use [def-sfb-moduli-chart-normalization]. Ordinary algebraic-space point classes are [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], with the atlas topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology] and the induced point maps and quasi-compactness predicate of [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. Ordinary properness of $f:E\to F$ means that every compatible scheme map $p:U\to V$ between etale charts $h_U\to E$ and $h_V\to F$ is locally of finite type, that $f$ is quasi-compact (every affine scheme base change has compact point space), that for every scheme $T$ and $a:h_T\to F$ the actual projection $E\times_F h_T\to h_T$ is closed on these ordinary point spaces, and that the presheaf diagonal $E\to E\times_F E$ is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion].
